title: Sell Mineral Rights in Edgewater, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Edgewater, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own coal or coalbed methane minerals near Edgewater, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for this former Jefferson County coal camp.
heroLead: Edgewater was built as a coal company town, one of several such communities scattered through northwestern Jefferson County, and its unincorporated status today doesn't erase the mineral title history that came with that origin.
intro: Company towns like Edgewater were typically built on land the mining operator already owned outright, mineral rights included, and as those company holdings were later sold off, subdivided, or passed to individuals, the mineral estate didn't always travel with the house or lot. If you've inherited property here, it's worth confirming whether your family's ownership includes the minerals or only the surface.
For owners who do hold the mineral estate, whether directly or through a relative who acquired it outside the company system, we buy those interests directly once ownership is confirmed.

sections.heading: A company town's mineral legacy
paragraphs: When coal operators sold off former company housing and land around Edgewater, the transactions sometimes retained mineral rights for the company or its successors, meaning a current homeowner may hold clear surface title without ever having acquired the minerals underneath at all.

sections.heading: Checking what you actually own
paragraphs: We start by reviewing the specific deed for an Edgewater-area property to determine whether it conveyed minerals along with the surface or reserved them separately. That answer shapes everything about whether there's an interest to sell in the first place.

sections.heading: Current activity and what it means for value
paragraphs: This part of Jefferson County sits on the play's flank rather than its dense core, so most confirmed interests here are valued against lease and permit comparables rather than an existing royalty stream. We check current records for the specific tract before discussing a range.

faqs.question: I own my house in Edgewater. Does that mean I automatically own the minerals under it?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Many former company-town lots were sold with the mineral rights reserved separately. We check your specific deed to confirm what you actually hold.

faqs.question: How do I find out who does hold the minerals if I don't?
faqs.answer: We can trace the chain of title from the original company sale forward through Jefferson County records to identify the current mineral owner, which may or may not be your family.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Edgewater?
faqs.answer: This area sits on the lighter-activity edge of the Black Warrior CBM play, so we check current permit records for the specific location before discussing value.

faqs.question: What if my deed doesn't mention minerals at all, one way or the other?
faqs.answer: We review the full chain of title, not only your most recent deed, since an earlier transaction in the chain may hold the answer.
